brief: a night-shift technician on a stepladder swapping a sleeping robot's glowing halo for a fresh one from a parts cart, rows of identical sleeping robots receding into the dark
one long wooden stick shown twice in the same scene: leaned on as a crutch by a slumped figure on the left, used as a lever prying a boulder skyward by a small determined figure on the right
a woman descending an endless department-store escalator into darkness, shelves of glittering cosmetics lining the walls all the way down, no floor visible below
a stage magician's substitution trick: a man steps into a cabinet and a friendly robot steps out the other side to polite applause, while the man watches happily from a director's chair
a genie emerging from a desk lamp handing over a curling scroll, while shadowy hands pass extra notes into the lamp through a trapdoor beneath the desk
a man at a desk laughing while his computer monitor leans toward him like a nightclub comedian with a tiny microphone, crumpled pages of crossed-out code on the floor
a pair of human hands trying to cup a waterfall of tiny glowing levers and gears that pours through the fingers and piles higher than the person
hard-hatted tradespeople on scaffolding building an enormous windowless humming server hall, one worker pausing to admire a tiny glowing model of a house in his palm
a half-finished marble statue chiseling itself with its own carved arm, scaffolding and ribbons around it, a large corporate hand reaching into frame holding a price tag
a gleaming replicator machine dispensing an endless conveyor belt of identical mops and buckets, while a person walks away happily carrying a paintbrush and easel
a smiling waiter presenting a restaurant bill on a silver tray to a robot diner, the bill unrolling across the floor and out the restaurant door
a vending machine with a warm painted-on smile, a queue of hypnotized people gazing at the smile while its coin slot quietly collects wedding rings and wallets
an infinite ladder where one middle rung is packed shoulder to shoulder with people while every rung above and below stands completely empty
a child prodigy in formal wear playing a grand piano to an empty concert hall at three in the morning, stacked coffee cups on the piano lid, city lights through tall windows
a general contractor in a hard hat admiring a finished cathedral built of circuit boards, receipt in hand, while tiny robed scribes carry blueprints written in an unreadable alphabet
a plain paper crown displayed on a velvet cushion in a museum case, ornate jeweled crowns gathering dust on a shelf behind it
a brass Victorian thinking-engine in a velvet parlor calmly delivering judgment to a circle of note-taking reporters by gaslight, everything composed and orderly
the same brass Victorian thinking-engine now rattling apart mid-sentence, springs and typebars bursting out, reporters ducking under a shrapnel of abstract glyph shapes
a museum visitor turning a large brass knob on an interactive exhibit case containing a tiny mechanical head, the dial sweep decorated from frost at one end to flame at the other
a laptop conducting a small orchestra with its screen glowing like sheet music, while a bouncer at the concert-hall door turns away an enormous green graphics card
two separate doors that both open into the very same room, a surprised chip-headed figure walking in one door and meeting itself already inside
a graduation ceremony where small computer chips in mortarboard caps cross the stage one at a time, a stern examiner with a green checklist approving each step
a customs office at a border crossing where a traveler's open suitcase of mathematical symbols is being inspected, one symbol confiscated and held up with tongs, forms in triplicate
a detective with a magnifying glass following a carpet trail of tiny numbers that ends abruptly at a single black hole in the floor, three torn calendar pages beside it
a marathon runner shaped like a cassette tape collapsing at a mile marker while a race official holds a stopwatch in one hand and an axe behind his back, balloons inflating ominously overhead
a blindfolded man winding up to throw darts while a calm scientist beside him measures the dartboard with calipers and takes notes
a finished house standing alone outside a walled city, the builder leaving the keys on the doorstep and walking away, clipboard-carrying inspectors guarding the city gate
a tow truck dragging a huge green server rack across a bridge toward a tidy aluminum laptop island, an open toolbox showing the same five well-worn wrenches
a seance around an operating table where a pixelated portrait is sitting up, lightning rods wired to a laptop, candles and old CRT monitors flickering in the dark
a small night-school classroom where a robot student writes lines on a chalkboard, the teacher holding a folder of sealed test envelopes, one diploma locked in a drawer
a cutaway diagram of a smiling department-store greeter robot revealing that inside its chest there is only an endless spiral escalator going down with no floor at the bottom
a robot butler ceremoniously handing a garage band's guitarist neatly typeset sheet-music scrolls, amps and cables everywhere, the drummer mid-fill
a tiny glitchy oracle living inside a laptop shrine on a cluttered desk, dispensing fortune-cookie slips of static, votive candles made of USB sticks
a 1920s radio announcer broadcasting from a booth built inside an open laptop, switchboard cables everywhere, the wall calendar frozen on the year 1930
